retained.name: confinement_ratio_entropy
retained.hypothesis: Adsorption entropy loss (per R) grows monotonically with the ratio of adsorbate van der Waals volume to the cubed pore-path diameter; systems where Vol approaches the pore volume lose translational/rotational freedom most, so including log(q_Vol / lsd_p**3) as a network input lowers MAE of s_ads/s_gas prediction compared with the 14 raw inputs alone.

retained.name: wall_contact_density
retained.hypothesis: Entropy loss increases with the wall-area density of the accessible pore space: frameworks presenting more accessible surface area (ASA, m^2/g) per unit accessible pore volume (AV, cm^3/g) confine guests to regions close to walls, suppressing translation and rotation. The dimensionless ratio q_ASA/q_AV, entered as a log, gives the network a compact surface-to-volume measure of the pore system that no single raw input carries, and reduces MAE of entropy-loss/R.

retained.name: confinement_to_volume_ratio
retained.hypothesis: Entropy loss scales with the specific surface contacted by the adsorbate, damped by adsorbate bulkiness and by path diameter: frameworks with high accessible area, small adsorbates, and narrow diffusion paths produce larger s_ads/s_gas deviations. Replacing raw Vol with this saturating ratio improves MAE over the 14-input network baseline.

retained.name: size_path_stiffness
retained.hypothesis: Entropy loss is governed by the square of the geometric mismatch between adsorbate span and the largest free-sphere path: adsorbates whose largest atom-to-atom distance approaches or exceeds the path diameter are forced into a small set of configurations, so s_ads/s_gas deviations grow quadratically as q_GeDi/q_lsd_p rises. Adding this stiffness ratio to the network reduces MAE of entropy loss/R below the 0.5405 baseline.

retained.name: winding_penalty
retained.hypothesis: Entropy loss increases with molecular shape anisotropy (PMI3/PMI1) combined with framework channel tortuosity, approximated by the ratio of largest free sphere to largest free-sphere-along-path (lsd_f/lsd_p < 1). Elongated molecules (large anisotropy) lose extra conformational/rotational entropy when threading tortuous or narrow-window channels; in wide-pore, low-tortuosity frameworks the anisotropy effect vanishes.

retained.name: window_aspect_gate
retained.hypothesis: Entropy loss is maximal when the molecule's largest atom-to-atom dimension (GeDi) slightly exceeds the path-window diameter (lsd_p) but fits the cavity (lsd_f): such 'threading' molecules must pass through narrow windows and pay a large configurational penalty, whereas molecules much smaller than lsd_p move freely and molecules larger than lsd_f are excluded or immobilized in single sites. The descriptor should peak in the regime lsd_p < GeDi < lsd_f. Inference only.

retained.name: occivol_per_mol
retained.hypothesis: The occupiable framework volume per unit adsorbate volume, normalized to reference medians, is the dominant single predictor of the entropy-loss fraction: across pure-silica frameworks and diverse adsorbates, 1 - s_ads/s_gas decreases monotonically with occivol_per_mol, and this descriptor alone explains more entropy-loss variance than any single native input. Source: Dauenhauer & Abdelrahman's occupiable-volume universality claim (R1E05); this instance is classified as a known_relation re-expressed in dimensionless, unit-safe form.

retained.name: wall_contact_intensity
retained.hypothesis: The accessible-surface-area-to-accessible-volume ratio, normalized by reference medians, acts as a confinement intensity measure that predicts entropy loss independently of pore size: frameworks with high surface area per unit accessible volume place every adsorbate configuration close to a confining wall, suppressing both translational (reduced free volume per configuration) and rotational (wall obstruction) freedom simultaneously. Entropy-loss fraction (1 - s_ads/s_gas) increases monotonically with q_ASA/q_AV, and the descriptor predicts the same entropy loss for a large-pore framework with tortuous narrow channels and a small-pore framework with open cages if their surface-to-volume ratios coincide — a degeneracy that lsd_f, lsd_p, AV, or density individually break but that the ratio collapses. Because ASA (m^2/g) and AV (cm^3/g) use different length scales, the reference normalization q_ASA/q_AV removes silent unit-conversion risk; the absolute numeric value carries the m^2/cm^3 scale consistently.

retained.name: inkbottle_path_mismatch_descriptor
retained.hypothesis: Entropy retention is maximal when the largest free-sphere diameter along the path (lsd_p) approaches the largest free sphere (lsd_f); a mismatch (lsd_p << lsd_f) indicates ink-bottle pores (R1E06) that add an entropic barrier beyond what cage size alone predicts, so the descriptor (q_lsd_p − q_lsd_f²/q_lsd_p) explains residual variance in entropy loss/R not captured by the individual lsd features.

retained.name: density_pore_volume_confinement_descriptor
retained.hypothesis: Entropy loss fraction increases with the joint action of high framework density and small accessible pore volume relative to molecular bulk: the descriptor predicts residual entropy loss/R beyond the raw 14 features because the product q_density * (Vol/AV) encodes a confinement-per-molecule-packing mechanism, whereas the network sees density and AV only as marginal inputs.

retained.name: window_shape_rigidity_descriptor
retained.hypothesis: The fraction of entropy retained depends on both the absolute free-sphere diameter and the ratio lsd_f/lsd_p (neck-to-cavity contrast): systems with large minimum(lsd_f, lsd_p) retain more entropy, but for very small lsd_f the 'ink-bottle' effect reverses the trend, so a descriptor combining min(lsd_f, lsd_p) with the contrast term will capture the U-shaped lsd_f dependence better than lsd_f alone.

retained.name: cavity_size_match_descriptor
retained.hypothesis: The fraction of entropy lost scales with the cube of the ratio of molecular van der Waals volume to the largest free sphere diameter, i.e. the fraction of the cavity volume occupied by the adsorbate itself: frameworks whose largest free sphere barely exceeds the molecular volume force near-fully hindered translation/rotation (loss approaching a fixed framework fraction, R2E05), while spacious cavities (FAU-like) retain entropy (R2E01, R2E02). A normalized volume-fill ratio should explain framework-to-framework slope differences (eta, R2E14) better than lsd_f alone, lowering MAE of entropy loss/R.

retained.name: confinement_gap_ratio
retained.hypothesis: If entropy retention is governed by how much free-path space the framework offers relative to the adsorbate's largest molecular dimension, then adding this single gap-ratio descriptor alongside the existing 14 inputs will reduce the MAE of (entropy loss)/R relative to the baseline network; it will not if the network has already saturated the information in lsd_p and GeDi separately.

retained.name: free_volume_capacity_ratio
retained.hypothesis: If entropy retention is governed by the ratio of the framework's probe-accessible pore volume per gram to the adsorbate's molecular van der Waals volume (a free-volume/capacity argument: more occupiable void per molecular size preserves translational entropy), then adding this descriptor to the 14-input baseline will reduce MAE of (entropy loss)/R; it will fail if the network already expresses the AV–Vol interaction implicitly.

retained.name: surface_interaction_index
retained.hypothesis: Entropy retention correlates with the ratio of framework accessible surface area per mass to the adsorbate's own surface area per volume, modulated by framework density: frameworks offering more surface area relative to the molecule's contact area (and at lower site density) provide shallower, less-restricting interaction fields that preserve entropy. Adding q_ASA*q_LabuteASA/(q_Vol*q_density) will reduce validation MAE of entropy loss/R versus baseline.

retained.name: asymmetric_inertia_confinement
retained.hypothesis: For anisotropic molecules, the rotational entropy lost upon confinement scales with the ratio of the largest to smallest principal moment of inertia (PMI3/PMI1, a prolate/asymmetry measure) divided by the confinement clearance given by the window diameter and molecular length: highly asymmetric molecules in tight windows have one nearly-free rotation about the long axis but fully frustrated rotations about the short axes, producing a distinct entropy-loss regime that isotropic-size descriptors miss. Including q_PMI3/(q_PMI1*q_lsd_p*q_GeDi) will reduce validation MAE of entropy loss/R versus baseline, with the largest gains for planar or elongated adsorbates in window-limited frameworks.

retained.name: surface_area_confinement
retained.hypothesis: Entropy retention scales with the accessible framework volume (per mass) normalized by the adsorbate surface area, so including q_AV/q_LabuteASA reduces MAE of entropy loss/R beyond the baseline network.

retained.name: rotational_inertia_confinement
retained.hypothesis: Rotational entropy loss is governed by the ratio of the adsorbate's largest principal moment of inertia to the square of the framework's largest free-sphere diameter; adding q_PMI3/(q_lsd_f**2) to the baseline network reduces MAE of entropy loss/R, with partial dependence showing larger entropy loss (higher 1-s_ads/s_gas) when this ratio is large.
